title: Saving for a shared goal, step by step
description: Flatmates, partners and friends saving toward something together do best with a clear target, a fair split and money kept separate.

body.heading: Agree the target in numbers
paragraphs: Shared goals fail most often on vagueness. Put a figure and a date on it: a holiday deposit of a set amount by a set month, a new sofa split three ways by spring. Once the total and deadline exist, the monthly amount is simple division, and everyone can judge whether it fits their budget.
It is far better to choose a modest target everyone can genuinely afford than an exciting one that quietly strains one person. Ask directly, and believe the answer.

body.heading: Decide what fair means
paragraphs: An equal split is simplest, but not always fairest when incomes differ widely. Some groups split in proportion to earnings; others split equally but let the better-off cover shared extras. There is no correct answer, only an answer everyone has honestly agreed to.
Write the agreement down somewhere shared, even just a message thread. Friendly arrangements survive on clarity, not on everyone remembering the conversation the same way.

body.heading: Keep the money boringly safe
paragraphs: Hold the fund in one clearly labelled account or pot, with one person keeping a simple shared record of what went in and out. Avoid mixing goal money with everyday spending, where it evaporates invisibly.
If someone's circumstances change, renegotiate early and kindly. Shared saving is a relationship first and a spreadsheet second; adjusting the plan beats silent resentment every time.

takeaway: Name the figure and the date, agree a split everyone can afford, and keep the fund separate with a shared record.
